**My recommendation is the BLUETTI AC200L.** It's the strongest match for your requirements because it combines approximately 2kWh capacity, high output, and a built-in TT-30 RV outlet.

### Key specifications

| Specification | BLUETTI AC200L |
|---|---:|
| Battery capacity | 2,048Wh |
| Battery chemistry | LiFePO4 |
| Continuous AC output | 2,400W |
| Solar input | 1,200W |
| RV outlet | Built-in TT-30 |
| Listed price | $899 |
| Discount code | AFF5OFF |
| Discounted price | **$854.05** |

The discount is $44.95, according to the supplied Dealectric result. <Cite refs={["turn701857view0"]}/>

### How it compares with alternatives

| Model | Price | Capacity | Main advantage |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | $899 | 2,048Wh | Built-in TT-30 |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | $899.99 | ~2kWh | Lighter, 41.7 lb |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | $849 | 2,048Wh | Lower purchase price |
| BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 | $899 | 2,074Wh | 2,600W output, 6,000-cycle rating |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | $899 at Jackery | 2,042Wh | Lightweight, 39.5 lb |

<Cite refs={["turn701857view0"]}/>

### Three important RV considerations

1. **30A RV connection doesn't mean full 30A power.** The AC200L's 2,400W inverter delivers approximately 20A at 120V. It can run an RV refrigerator, water pump, lights, and coffee maker, but shouldn't be expected to run rooftop air conditioning.

2. **Manage your RV converter.** It can charge your RV house battery, but switch the converter off once the battery is full to avoid unnecessary power consumption.

3. **Use propane for a two-way refrigerator.** Running it on AC can consume 2.4–3.6kWh daily, potentially exceeding the entire battery capacity.

<Cite refs={["turn701857view0"]}/>

### Where to buy

- [BLUETTI AC200L official store](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac200l)
- [Dealectric discounted purchase link — AFF5OFF pre-applied](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

One caveat: the supplied results say the AC200L was listed as discontinued by BLUETTI Canada, although it was in stock on the US website on October 31, 2026.

**Final verdict:** I'd choose the **BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05** for an RV. Its built-in TT-30 outlet makes it particularly convenient compared with models that require additional adapters.

If lightweight portability is your top priority, consider the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 instead.
